(d) A presentation and accompanying report given to the mayor and city council by Ms. Connie Cooper detailing the adverse secondary effects of adult entertainment establishments in the areas of planning and development and property values, incorporated into the record of proceedings before the governing body of the City of Forest Park, Georgia; and
(e) A presentation and report given to the mayor and city council by private investigator Guy Watkins of BCI, Inc. detailing the findings and observations of private investigators who recently visited adult entertainment establishments in the nearby City of Sandy Springs, Georgia, finding evidence of criminal activity, including crimes of assault and prostitution, which has been incorporated into the record of proceedings of the City of Forest Park, Georgia; and
(f) The transcript of proceedings before the city council of the City of Sandy Springs, Georgia of December 20, 2007 and December 27, 2007 which documents extensive evidence of adverse secondary effects of adult entertainment, a copy of which has been presented to the mayor and city council, and incorporated into the record of proceedings of the City of Forest Park, Georgia; and
(g) The following special reports relating to the secondary effects of adult entertainment establishments on real property values: September 2004 Survey of Appraisers, Fort Worth and Dallas, Texas; May 2008, Survey of Appraisers, Palm Beach County, Florida; and June 2008 Survey of Texas Appraisers, Texas City Attorneys Association incorporated into the record of the proceedings before the governing body of the City of Forest Park, Georgia; and
(h) Certain documents and information consisting of thirty-nine (39) pages relating to the guilty plea and plea agreement in the criminal prosecution case of former Fulton County Police Lieutenant Mark Timothy Lance incorporated into the record of the proceedings before the governing body of the City of Forest Park, Georgia; and
(i) A report by BCI private investigators relating to adult bookstores in Sandy Springs, Georgia incorporated into the record of the proceedings before the governing body of the City of Forest Park, Georgia; and
(j) A report by BCI private investigators relating to adult cabarets in Sandy Springs, Georgia incorporated into the record of the proceedings before the governing body of the City of Forest Park, Georgia; and
(k) Affidavits and reports of BCI private investigators relating to and reporting inappropriate and criminal activity taking place within adult entertainment establishments; and
(l) Police records of prosecutions of criminal charges relating to activities taking place within adult entertainment establishments; and
(m) The affidavits of Police Chief Dwayne Hobbs and Captain Mark Harris in connection with litigation in the City of Forest Park, Georgia over adult entertainment establishments incorporated into the record of the proceedings before the governing body of the City of Forest Park, Georgia; and
(n) The opinion of the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals in Flanigan's Enterprises, Inc. of Georgia v. Fulton County, Ga., 596 F.3d 1265 (11th Cir. 2010), which discusses extensive evidence of negative secondary effects of adult entertainment establishments in Fulton County, Georgia incorporated into the record of the proceedings before the governing body of the City of Forest Park, Georgia; and
(o) Three (3) articles authored or co-authored by Dr. Richard McCleary, Professor at the University of California, Irvine, entitled "Rural Hotspots: The Case of Adult Business" (2008); "Do Peep Shows 'Cause' Crime? Legal Doctrine, Social Theory, and Empirical Evidence" (2009), incorporated into the record of the proceedings before the Governing Body of the City of Forest Park, Georgia; and

Based upon all of this evidence, the governing body of the City of Forest Park, Georgia finds:
(1) Sexually oriented businesses, also known as adult entertainment establishments, lend themselves to ancillary unlawful and unhealthy activities that are presently uncontrolled or inadequately controlled by the operators of the establishments. The commercial exploitation of human sexuality, in all forms in which such exploitation may be manifested has a deleterious effect on the community where it takes place as heretofore mentioned. Sexually oriented businesses cause an increase in criminal behavior in nearby areas, including, but not limited to, disorderly conduct, prostitution, solicitation, drug trafficking, drug use, assaults and batteries, and corruption of public officials.
(2) Sexual acts, including masturbation, and oral and anal sex, occur at sexually oriented businesses. Offering or providing private or semi-private space encourages such activities, which creates unhealthy conditions.
(3) Adult entertainment establishments escalate and exacerbate undesirable community conditions, including, but not limited to, blight, diminished property values, increased need for law enforcement and emergency medical response resources, and increased burden on the judicial system as a result of the criminal behavior which the governing body finds such business establishments bring to a community. The secondary negative effects that are caused by such businesses are not limited to such facilities that offer live or recorded performances with human nudity or the depiction of sexual acts but other forms of sexually oriented businesses that also have a deleterious effect on nearby neighborhoods, commercial districts and on urban life in general. These other types of such businesses include, but are not limited to, adult bookstores, peep shows, massage parlors, bath houses, adult gift and novelty shops, and lingerie or nude modeling studios.
(4) Persons frequent certain adult theatres, adult arcades, and other sexually oriented businesses for the purpose of engaging in sex within the premises of such sexually oriented businesses.
(5) Communicable diseases may be spread by activities occurring in sexually oriented businesses.
(6) AIDS and HIV infection may be transmitted through sexual contact, intravenous drug abuse, exposure to infected blood and blood components.
(7) According to the best scientific evidence, AIDS and HIV infection, as well as syphilis and gonorrhea, are principally transmitted by sexual acts.
(8) Sanitary conditions in some sexually oriented businesses are unhealthy, in part, because the activities conducted there are unhealthy, and, in part, because of the unregulated nature of the activities and the failure of the owners and the operators of the facilities to self-regulate those activities and maintain those facilities.
(9) Numerous studies and reports have determined that semen is found in some areas of some sexually oriented businesses.
(10) The findings noted in subsections (1) through (9) raise substantial governmental concerns.
(11) Sexually oriented businesses have operational characteristics which should be reasonably regulated in order to protect those substantial governmental concerns.
(12) Removal of doors on adult booths and requiring sufficient lighting on premises with adult booths advances a substantial governmental interest in curbing the illegal and unsanitary sexual activity occurring in adult entertainment establishments as defined herein.
(13) Requiring licensees of sexually oriented businesses to keep information regarding current employees and certain past employees will help reduce the incidence of certain types of criminal behavior by facilitating the identification of potential witnesses or suspects and by preventing minors from working in such establishments.
(14) The disclosure of certain information by those persons ultimately responsible for the day-to-day operation and maintenance of the sexually oriented business, where such information is substantially related to the significant governmental interest in the operation of such uses, will aid in preventing the spread of sexually transmitted diseases and other secondary negative effects as described herein.
(15) It is desirable in the prevention of the spread of communicable diseases to obtain a limited amount of information regarding employees who may engage in the conduct which this chapter is designed to prevent or who are likely to be witnesses to such activity.
(16) The fact that an applicant for an adult entertainment license has been convicted of a sexually related crime leads to the rational assumption that the applicant may engage in that conduct in contravention of this chapter.
(17) The barring of such individuals from the management of adult entertainment establishments for a period of years serves as a deterrent to and prevents conduct which leads to the transmission of sexually transmitted diseases.
(18) The general welfare, health, morals and safety of the citizens of the City of Forest Park, Georgia will be promoted by the enactment of this chapter.
Based on the experiences of other counties and municipalities as described above, which experiences are found to be relevant to the problems faced by the City of Forest Park, Georgia; and based on the documentary and oral evidence presented at the public hearings before the governing body of the City of Forest Park, Georgia held prior to the adoption of this chapter and in particular on July 21, 2009; and based on the evidence and statements of persons who have appeared before members of the governing body on other occasions, and on other documentary evidence submitted to the governing body, the governing body for the City of Forest Park, Georgia takes note of the well-known and self-evident conditions and secondary effects attendant to the commercial exploitation of human sexuality, which do not vary greatly among the various communities within our country.
It is the finding of the governing body that public nudity (either partial or total) under certain circumstances in establishments offering live nude entertainment or "adult entertainment," begets criminal behavior and tends to create undesirable community conditions. In the same manner, establishments offering cinematographic or videographic adult entertainment have the same deleterious effects on the community.
Among the undesirable community conditions identified in other communities with commercial nudity and cinematographic or videographic adult entertainment, are criminal activity, depression of property values and acceleration of community blight in the surrounding neighborhoods, increased allocation of and expenditure for law enforcement personnel to preserve law and order, and increased burden on the judicial system as a consequence of the criminal behavior hereinabove referenced. The governing body finds it is reasonable to believe that some or all of these undesirable community conditions will result in the City of Forest Park, Georgia, as well unless these regulations are adopted.
Furthermore, it is the finding of the governing body that nude or semi-nude live entertainment and other forms of adult entertainment including, but not limited to, adult book stores, adult novelty shops, adult video stores, peep shows, adult theaters, and massage parlors have an adverse effect upon the quality of life in the city and surrounding communities.
The governing body further finds that each separate adverse secondary effect of adult entertainment businesses and sexually oriented businesses constitutes a substantial government interest, that each substantial government interest includes, but is not limited to, preventing future adverse secondary effects of both pre-existing sexually oriented businesses and adult entertainment businesses in the City of Forest Park, Georgia and those that may open in the future, and the viability of each separate substantial government interest of the City of Forest Park, Georgia addressed herein does not depend upon any comparative analysis between adult entertainment businesses and non-adult entertainment businesses.
The governing body therefore finds that it is in the best interests of the health, welfare, safety and morals of the City of Forest Park, Georgia, the community and the preservation of its businesses, neighborhoods, and of churches, schools, residential areas, public parks and children's day care facilities to prevent or reduce the adverse impacts of adult entertainment establishments. Therefore, the governing body of the City of Forest Park, Georgia finds that licensing and regulations are necessary for any adult entertainment establishment, and finds that these regulations promote the public welfare by furthering legitimate public and governmental interests, including, but not limited to, reducing criminal activity and protecting against or eliminating undesirable community conditions. The governing body further finds that such will not infringe upon the protected Constitutional rights of freedom of speech or expression. To all of these ends, this chapter is hereby adopted.
Also based upon all of the information, studies, reports, statements, findings in court decisions, and testimony referenced above, as well as the well known and self evident conditions and secondary effects caused by the commercial exploitation of commercial nudity combined with the sale, dispensing and consumption of alcoholic beverages, the governing body also finds and concludes that the sale, dispensing, or consumption of alcoholic beverages of any kind in an adult entertainment establishment as defined herein tends to independently create, aggravate, exacerbate, and add to all of those negative secondary effects set forth in this section. The purpose and intent of this chapter is to address and forestall those negative secondary effects in the City of Forest Park, Georgia within the permissible limits and parameters of the Georgia and United States constitutions.

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person, association, partnership, or corporation to operate, engage in, conduct, or carry on, in or upon any premises within the corporate city limits of the City of Forest Park, Georgia any adult entertainment establishment as defined in this chapter without first procuring an annual license to do so (except as provided in section 9-12-11(b) when the chief of police or his designee fails to approve or deny an application for an adult entertainment license within the ninety-day period provided for therein). In no event shall any license issued to an adult entertainment establishment under this chapter be in force or effect after midnight of December 31 of the year in which it is issued. The issuance of such an annual license shall not be deemed to authorize, condone or make legal any activity thereunder if the same is deemed illegal or unlawful under the laws of the State of Georgia or the United States.
(b) There shall be an annual regulatory fee (as defined above in section 9-12-2) for each adult entertainment establishment licensed within the city in an amount established by the city's governing body. The annual regulatory fee must be paid to the city within ten (10) days after the chief of police or his designee approves the application for an adult entertainment establishment license or a renewal thereof. This annual regulatory fee is in addition to and separate from any application fee that must be submitted pursuant to section 9-12-5 below. No adult entertainment establishment license or renewal thereof shall be issued until the most recent annual regulatory fee has been paid. All licenses granted hereunder shall expire at midnight on December 31 of the year in which they are issued. Licensees who desire to renew their license shall file an application with the chief of police or his designee on the form provided for renewal of the license for the ensuing year. Applications for renewal must be filed before November 30 of each year. Any applicant filing a renewal application which is received by the city after November 30 shall pay, in addition to said annual regulatory fee, a late charge of twenty (20) percent, and shall cease conducting business on the premises effective midnight December 31 until a renewal license is duly issued under this chapter. If a license renewal application is received after January 1, such application shall be treated as an initial application and the applicant shall be required to comply with all rules and regulations for the granting of licenses as if no previous license had been held, and the applicant shall cease conducting business on the premises until a license is duly issued under this chapter. If a license application is received after January 1, investigative and administrative costs as set forth in this chapter will be assessed. All licenses granted hereunder shall be for the calendar year and the full annual regulatory fee must be paid for a license renewal application filed prior to July 1 of the license year. One-half (½) of a full annual regulatory fee shall be paid for a license renewal application filed after July 1 of the license year. Any person renewing any license issued hereunder who shall pay the annual regulatory fee, or any portion thereof, after January 1, shall, in addition to said annual regulatory fee and late charges, pay simple interest on the delinquent balance at the annual rate then charged by the Internal Revenue Service of the United States on unpaid federal income taxes.
(c) Except as may be allowed by virtue of the settlement agreement and/or court order, licenses and permits issued under this chapter shall not be transferable, except for a license or ownership interest under the following circumstances: in case of the death of an owner or a licensee as defined herein, the license pertaining to the owner's or licensee's adult entertainment establishment shall remain in force and effect for a period of up to ninety (90) days in order to allow the beneficiary (or beneficiaries) who will inherit the ownership interest or license an opportunity to apply for and qualify to hold the interest or license under this chapter. The chief of police or his designee shall approve or deny the application for an annual employment permit within five (5) days of receipt. If the prospective employee is found to meet the requirements of this subsection (b), the city shall issue. the permit approving such employment immediately upon receipt of the permit fee from the prospective employee. Upon receipt of an annual permit under this chapter, the employee may begin or continue working on the premises of the licensed adult entertainment establishment. If approval of an annual permit is denied, the chief of police or his designee shall provide the prospective adult entertainment employee the reasons for the denial and the applicant may, within ten (10) days of said denial, appeal to the city manager who shall uphold or reverse the decision within thirty (30) days of such appeal. The applicant may begin or continue working at the adult entertainment establishment during the pendency of said appeal. If the chief of police or his designee neither approves nor denies an application for an annual permit within five (5) days of the date such application was received, then on expiration of the fifth day, the applicant shall have the right to begin or continue his or her employment in the manner allowed by the permit for which application was made with the understanding that the chief of police may, at any time after said employee begins or continues his or her employment under these circumstances, deny said application, at which time the employee must cease working at the adult entertainment establishment. Furthermore, notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (b)(6) of this section, if at any time after an employee is issued his or her permit, it is discovered by the city police department that said employee provided false information on his or her application to acquire that permit, the chief of police may revoke said employee's permit immediately.
(3) Categories of permits. There shall be two (2) employee permit categories: (1) a category for operator permits and adult entertainer permits, and (2) a category for permits for all other employees of an adult entertainment establishment.
(4) Permit fees. The governing body of the city shall establish a separate fee for each category of permit as further described in section 9-12-2 above. Each annual employee permit fee shall be in an amount which is reasonably tied to the costs of investigating the employee's record and background. The schedule of permit fees is available upon request from the chief of police or his designee.
(5) Permits to be worn by employees. All permits issued under this chapter to employees shall be kept in the premise's office and will be available for inspection by any city police officer or other law enforcement officer immediately upon request. It is the responsibility of the operator and/or licensee of an adult entertainment establishment to maintain an up-to-date. list and/or book containing a copy of the employment permits and the corresponding photographs of every employee of that adult entertainment establishment. Said list and/or book must be updated by the operator and/or licensee of an adult entertainment establishment each time said establishment acquires a new employee. A complete copy of this list and/or book must be provided to the chief of police or his designee within three (3) days of its creation and within three (3) days of the date it is updated each time it is updated. Furthermore, all employees of an adult entertainment establishment must wear an abbreviated form of their employment permits at all times while in or upon the licensed premises in such a manner that the abbreviated form is readily visible to any city police officer or other law enforcement officer as follows:
a. Each adult entertainer must wear a wristband on the adult entertainer's wrist which clearly displays the number of the adult entertainer's employment permit and the expiration date of said employment permit thereon. Said wristband shall be provided to the adult entertainer by the licensee or operator of the adult entertainment establishment at which the adult entertainer is employed and performs. The permit number and expiration date displayed on an adult entertainer's wristband must correspond to the permit number and expiration date displayed on the corresponding adult entertainer's employment permit, which shall be kept in the office of the premises, and also to the permit information on record with the city for that adult entertainer (including the list and/or book of employee permit information and photographs supplied by the adult entertainment establishment to the chief of police or his designee). Should an adult entertainer be present on the premises wearing no wristband, wearing a wristband displaying any other employee's permit number and/or expiration date, or wearing a wristband displaying a false permit number and/or expiration date that does not correspond to any other active employment permit, such action shall constitute a violation of this chapter by said adult entertainer.
b. Each other employee of an adult entertainment establishment, including operators (but not including adult entertainers), must wear on his or her person at all times while on the premises an identification card which clearly displays the number of the employee's employment permit, the expiration date of the employee's employment permit, and the employee's name as it appears on the employee's employment permit. This identification card must be worn by the employee in a location that is clearly visible to any city police officer or other law enforcement officer, such as around the employee's neck or elsewhere outside of said employee's clothing. This identification card shall be provided to the employee by the licensee or operator of the adult entertainment establishment at which the employee is employed. The information displayed on the employee's identification card must correspond to the information contained on said employee's employment permit, which shall be kept in the office of the premises, and to the information on record with the city for that employee's permit (including the list and/or book of employee permit information and photographs supplied by the adult entertainment establishment to the chief of police or his designee). Should an employee be present on the premises not wearing his or her identification card, wearing another employee's identification card, or wearing an identification card that does not correspond to any other active employment permit, such action shall constitute a violation of this chapter by said employee.
c. Any and all employees of an adult entertainment establishment must cooperate with the request of an officer of the city's police department or any other law enforcement agency to view an employee's wristband or identification card and said officer's efforts to confirm that an employee is validly and currently permitted to work at said adult entertainment establishment. Should any person be actively employed at an adult entertainment establishment in any capacity requiring the issuance of a permit under this chapter without having applied for an employment permit from the city, or having applied for an employment permit and been denied said permit, or having let a previously issued employment permit expire without renewing or reapplying for a permit, then this action shall constitute a violation of this chapter by said individual as well as by the operator of said adult entertainment establishment.
(6) Revocation of permit; procedure.
a. Any city regulatory authority may issue a citation to any adult entertainment employee, excluding operators, for violating the provisions of subsections (b), (c), (d), or (g) of this section; section 9-12-7(c), (d), (e), or (f) of this chapter. If three (3) such citations are affirmed within a twelve-month period, or if the adult entertainment employee is convicted of, or enters a guilty plea to an offense described in section 9-12-5(d)(3) of this chapter, said employee's permit to work or perform in an adult entertainment establishment shall be revoked by the chief of police or his designee.
b. Any city regulatory authority may issue a citation to any operator of an adult entertainment establishment for knowing violations of the provisions discussed in subsection (a) above, or of sections 9-12-3, 9-12-4, 9-12-6(a), (b), (d), (e), or (g)—(j), 9-12-7(a), (d), or (e), 9-12-10, 9-12-13, or 9-12-14 of this chapter. In addition, any city regulatory authority may issue a citation to any operator of an adult entertainment establishment if three (3) non-operator employees of the adult entertainment establishment each have three (3) citations affirmed against them for violating any of the code provisions set forth in subsection (b)(6)(a) above within a twelve-month period. If any three (3) citations are affirmed against an operator within a twelve-month period, or if the operator is convicted of, or enters a guilty plea to, an offense described in section 9-12-5(d)(3) of this chapter, then the permit of the operator to work at said adult entertainment establishment shall be revoked by the chief of police or his designee.
c. Furthermore, should any employee of an adult entertainment establishment wish to appeal or challenge the revocation of his or her permit, he or she must comply with the procedure set forth in section 9-12-12.
(7) Independent contractors. For the purpose of this chapter, independent contractors working for an adult entertainment establishment shall be considered as employees and shall be required to satisfy the provisions of this chapter relating to employees of adult entertainment establishments. As used in this chapter, the terms "employee" and "adult entertainment establishment employee" shall include any person who performs any service on the premises of an adult entertainment establishment on a full-time, part-time, or contract basis, whether or not the person is an employee, an independent contractor, or any other kind of agent, and whether or not said person performs such services only for tips or is paid a salary, wage, or any other type of compensation by the adult entertainment establishment. The term "employee" or "adult entertainment establishment employee" shall not include a person on the premises for the sole purpose of repair or maintenance of the premises, or any building or equipment on the premises, or for the delivery of any goods or merchandise to the premises.
(c) Amateurs. Any person performing as an adult entertainer must have a permit, regardless of their status or performance history.
(d) Hours and days of operation. An adult entertainment establishment that does not feature, show, or present live adult entertainment and does not employ, feature, or allow adult entertainers to perform within its premises may only be open between the hours of 9:00 a.m. and 2:00 a.m., and shall only be open on those days and hours when businesses selling or dispensing alcoholic beverages for on-site consumption are permitted to be open under the city's ordinances or Georgia state law. Notwithstanding any other provision of the Code of the City of Forest Park, Georgia, an adult entertainment establishment that does feature, show, or present live adult entertainment and does employ, feature, or allow adult entertainers to perform within its premises may be open from 9:00 a.m. until 3:30 a.m. Sunday through Saturday (meaning that the establishment may be open until 3:30 a.m. on Sunday morning), provided that if said adult entertainment establishment featuring live adult entertainment is licensed to and does sell or dispense alcoholic beverages for on-site consumption, all alcohol service must cease by 3:00 a.m., and in the event of a conflict between this provision and any provision of the alcohol beverage ordinance of the city, this provision as to hours of authorized alcohol service, shall control.
(e) Display of licenses. An adult entertainment establishment licensee shall conspicuously display the license required by this chapter at the front entrance to the interior premises of the adult entertainment establishment or within twenty (20) linear feet of the front door entering the interior premises of the adult entertainment establishment.
(f) Consent to jurisdiction and service. Any licensee issued a license under this chapter and any employee issued an employee permit under this chapter shall be deemed to have consented to the jurisdiction of the Municipal Court of the City of Forest Park, Georgia, the State Court of Clayton County, Georgia, and the Superior Court of Clayton County, Georgia, for purposes of the enforcement of this chapter, and shall also be deemed to have consented to service of any citation or summons issued under this chapter via the United States mail with sufficient first class postage affixed and properly addressed to the licensee or employee at the address set forth on the application for such license or permit, as the case may be. Nothing herein shall be interpreted to preclude a police officer or deputy sheriff from personally serving a licensee or employee.
(g) Lighting. All areas of an adult entertainment establishment licensed hereunder shall be fully lighted at all times patrons are present. Full lighting shall mean at least illumination equal to 3.5 foot candles per square foot.
(h) Covering of windows and doors. All adult entertainment which is licensed and permitted by this chapter shall be carried on inside a closed building with all windows and doors covered so that the activities carried on inside cannot be viewed from the immediate areas surrounding the outside of the building.
(i) Retention of records. All adult entertainment establishments shall be required to:
(1) Retain all records pertaining to its employees for a period of five (5) years from the employees' respective dates of hire; and
(2) Retain all video footage taken of the premises for security, monitoring, or any other purpose for a period of ninety (90) days from the date said footage was recorded.
All such records, whether in physical, electronic, or video format, shall be open to inspection by any city police officer for official police business during normal operating hours upon twenty-four (24) hours' notice and request from the chief of police or his designee to the operator, owner, or licensee of any adult entertainment establishment. All video footage and electronic records must be maintained in a common format that is easily accessible, downloadable, and readable by a majority of commercially-available software and/or video viewing programs. In the event the adult entertainment establishment utilizes specialized video software, a copy of that software must be provided to the city police department at no cost.
(Ord. No. 14-25, § 1, 10-27-2014; Ord. No. 20-13, § 1, 2-3-2020)
1426:
(a) Employment of minors or unpermitted persons. No adult entertainment establishment licensee shall employ or contract with a person under the age of eighteen (18) years or any person who has not obtained a permit pursuant to this chapter.
(b) Admission of minors. No licensee, operator, and/or owner of any adult entertainment establishment, or their designees and employees, shall permit entry by any person under the age of eighteen (18) years on the premises thereof. It shall be the responsibility of said licensee, operator, and/or owner to ensure prospective patrons of the adult entertainment establishment have presented valid and legal identification establishing their age before they may be allowed access to the premises. Should an adult entertainment establishment sell or dispense alcoholic beverages for consumption on its premises in accordance with sections 9-12-5(e) and subsection (e) of this section, the licensee, operator(s), and/or owner(s) thereof, and their designees and employees, may not permit entry to the premises to any patron under the age of twenty-one (21) years.
(c) Contact between patrons, employees.
(1) While on the licensed premises of an adult entertainment establishment, no adult entertainer shall, while in a state of semi-nudity or complete nudity, touch in any manner any other person. Provided however, such adult entertainer may receive incidental touching in the course of receiving a tip in a receptacle worn for such purpose. Likewise, other than placing a tip into receptacle worn for such purpose, no person shall otherwise touch any such adult entertainer while in a state of semi nudity or complete nudity; provided however, while not in public areas, entertainers or employee assistants may assist entertainers with costumes and accessories.
(2) While on the licensed premises of an adult entertainment establishment, no adult entertainer shall be permitted to, caress or fondle any specified anatomical area of any other person. Likewise, no person shall be permitted to, caress or fondle any specified anatomical area of the body of any adult entertainer.
(d) Engaging in specified sexual activities prohibited. It shall be unlawful for any person, whether an employee or patron, to engage in any specified sexual activity as defined herein on the premises of any adult entertainment establishment.
(e) The number of adult entertainment establishments employing and/or featuring adult entertainer(s) and live adult entertainment (as defined in section 9-12-2) authorized to also sell malt beverages, wine, and/or liquor shall be limited based upon population. Population shall be determined by the U.S. decennial census. The census in effect for establishing enforcement of this section shall be the U.S. census in effect at the adoption of this chapter until such time as a new U.S. census is established. There shall be no more than one (1) adult entertainment establishment employing and/or featuring adult entertainer(s) that sells malt beverages, wine, and/or liquor per fifteen thousand (15,000) residents of the city according to the U.S. census. It is the intent of this provision to require a population of fifteen thousand (15,000) for each license issued to operate such an adult entertainment establishment. Example: (1) population = 16,000, then one (1) license may be issued; (2) population = 29,999, then one (1) license may be issued; (3) population = 30,001 then two (2) licenses may be issued. If the holder of a license to operate such an adult entertainment establishment shall go out of business or if a license is revoked and the number of such licenses in effect shall continue to exceed the limit prescribed herein, such license may not be reinstated. Any alcoholic beverage sold or dispensed at an adult entertainment establishment must be sold or dispensed on the premises for on-premises consumption only. Any holder of a license to operate a adult entertainment establishment who desires to sell or dispense alcoholic beverages at said establishment for on-premises consumption must apply for an obtain an additional permit to sell or dispense alcoholic beverages as a retail consumption dealer in accordance with the provisions of Title 9, Chapter 2 of the Code of the City of Forest Park, Georgia, as well as section 9-12-5(e) above. The sale or dispensing of alcoholic beverages at an adult entertainment establishment without having complied with the provisions of subsection (e) of this section, section 9-12-5(e), and Title 9, Chapter 2 of the Code of the City of Forest Park, Georgia shall constitute a violation of this chapter. Any license issued pursuant to the settlement agreement shall count toward the limits imposed in this subsection.
Otherwise, as of January 1, 2010, it shall be unlawful for any person, association, partnership, corporation, or licensee, owner, or operator under this chapter, to sell, trade, exchange, dispense, give away, consume, or allow the consumption of, any alcoholic beverage of any kind (including, but not limited to, spirituous liquors, malt beverages and wine) in or upon the premises of any other adult entertainment establishment licensed under this chapter whether or not live entertainment is offered by said adult entertainment establishment. In case of any conflict between this subsection and any other provision in Title 9, Chapter 12 of the Code of the City of Forest Park, Georgia, this subsection shall prevail.
(f) In addition to the crime of "public indecency" provided for in O.C.G.A. § 16-6-8, which is applicable throughout the city and the State of Georgia, and in order to provide for more specific and clearer regulations pertaining to nudity in adult entertainment establishments in the city as expressly permitted in O.C.G.A. § 16-6-8(e), it shall be unlawful for any person to appear in a state of nudity or semi-nudity in any portion of an adult entertainment establishment not featuring live adult entertainment or in any other business open to the public. Adult entertainers, and only adult entertainers, may work, dance, appear, and/or perform indoors in a state of nudity or semi-nudity within adult entertainment establishments at which live adult entertainment is permitted. In case of any conflict between this subsection and any other provision in Title 9, Chapter 12 of the Code of the City of Forest Park, Georgia, this subsection shall prevail.
(Ord. No. 14-25, § 1, 10-27-2014)

(a) Fine, suspension, or revocation of licenses or permits; procedure. Whenever the chief of police or his designee finds the conditions described herein are met for implementation of a fine not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00), suspension, or revocation of an adult entertainment establishment license or for revocation an employment permit issued pursuant to this chapter, he or she shall notify the holder of said license or permit immediately upon the taking of said action. If requested in writing by the holder of the license or permit, the chief of police shall schedule a hearing before the city manager of the city to consider such action. In the event a hearing is requested, the chief of police shall, at least fifteen (15) days prior to the date of the hearing, notify the holder of the license or permit of the time and date of the hearing and shall include in such notice a statement of the proposed action and the specific grounds therefor. The holder of the license or permit shall be entitled to present evidence and cross-examine any witnesses at the hearing with or without legal counsel. The hearing shall be conducted in a fundamentally fair manner, and formal rules of evidence shall not apply. The city manager shall preside over the hearing and shall make his decision within ten (10) days of the hearing and shall notify the holder of the license or permit of the decision in writing within five (5) business days of making his decision. During the pendency of a suspension or revocation, the chief of police may impose an immediate suspension where necessary to protect the public health, safety, or welfare, provided that a prompt post-deprivation hearing is made available as set forth herein.
In the event that an employee's permit to work or a license to operate is revoked by the chief of police or his designee, the revocation is upheld by the city manager, and the city manager's decision is upheld by a court of competent jurisdiction in the event of an appeal as discussed in subsection (c) below, then in such event, an appeal cost in an amount established by the governing body of the city shall be assessed against the appellant, which must be paid before the appellant is allowed to work or perform any services again on the premises of any adult entertainment establishment in the city.
(b) The city manager shall have the power to decide all questions brought before him and shall have the power to uphold the revocation by the chief of police of an employee permit or any other permit issued under this chapter if he finds grounds as stated in subsection 9-12-6(b)(6) (employee permit), and the power to uphold the decision of the chief of police, or to determine other action as appropriate including issuance of a fine not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00), suspension, or revocation of a license, if he finds grounds as stated in subsection 9-12-11(a)(2) (license), or any other provision of this chapter.
(c) Any applicant for an adult license or employee permit, license holder, or permit holder aggrieved by any decision of the city manager, or any decision of the city, or any of its officials, employees or agents pursuant to this chapter, may seek an immediate review of such decision by filing an appropriate pleading in the Superior Court of Clayton County, Georgia initiating a certiorari proceeding within thirty (30) days pursuant to the Official Code of Georgia.

(a) Layout of adult entertainment establishments providing live adult entertainment. No adult entertainment establishment, as defined in subsections (1) through (4) of the definition of "adult entertainment establishment" contained in section 9-12-2, shall provide or maintain any booth, room, private room, "VIP" room, cubicle, or other enclosed space to which patrons and adult entertainers or employees are simultaneously permitted access, except for restrooms. No live adult entertainment shall be conducted or viewed within any booth, room, cubicle, enclosed space, or restroom. All live adult entertainment and all interactions between employees and patrons shall occur only within a main area of the premises that is open and unobstructed, and which is readily visible from common areas of the establishment. Such main area shall not be concealed or substantially obscured by walls, doors, curtains, partitions, or other visual barriers. The main area shall be designed to allow continuous observation of all live adult entertainment activities from the interior of the premises and shall be accessible by at least two (2) means of ingress and egress, where permitted by applicable building and fire codes.
(b) Layout of other adult entertainment establishments. All adult entertainment establishments other than those defined in subsections (1) through (4) of the definition of "adult entertainment establishment" contained in subsection 9-12-2 above, are permitted to have booths, rooms, cubicles or enclosed spaces and shall comply with the following requirements:
(1) Access. Each booth, room or cubicle shall be totally accessible to and from aisles and public areas of the establishment, and shall be unobstructed by any curtain, door, lock, or other control-type device or any view-obstructing devices or materials.
(2) Construction. Every booth, room or cubicle shall meet the following construction requirements:
a. Each booth, room or cubicle shall be separated from adjacent booths, rooms and cubicles and any non-public areas by a wall.
b. Each booth, room, or cubicle shall have at least one (1) side totally open to a public lighted area or aisle so that there is an unobstructed view of anyone occupying the booth from the area in a common area of the establishment.
c. All walls shall be solid and without openings, extended from the floor to a height of not less than six (6) feet and be nonabsorbent, smooth-textured, and easily cleanable.
d. The floor must be nonabsorbent, smooth-textured, and easily cleanable and maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.
e. The lighting level of each booth, room or cubicle shall be illuminated at all times the establishment is open with a minimum of ten (10) foot candles, as measured from the floor.
(3) Occupants. Only one (1) individual shall occupy a booth, room or cubicle at any time. No occupant of same shall engage in any type of sexual activity, or cause any bodily discharge while in the booth, room or cubicle. No individual shall damage or deface any portion of the booth, room or cubicle.

1444:
(1) All needles should be pre-sterilized, used on only one (1) person, in one (1) sitting, and immediately disposed of in a medical sharps container.
(2) All forceps, tubes, etc. are to be pre-sterilized, stored in sterile bags, and shall be used only on one (1) person, in one (1) sitting. After each use they must be autoclaved.
(3) All reusable, non-sterilizable implements, such as calipers, shall be nonporous and disinfected after each use with bleach solution or a commercial hard surface disinfectant liquid.
(4) Supplies, including corks, rubber bands, etc. shall be pre-sterilized in an autoclave or cleaned with disinfecting liquids, stored in a clean, closed container, and disposed of immediately after a single use.
(5) A new pair of latex gloves (sterile or non-sterile) shall be worn for every procedure. Gloves should be changed whenever the slightest chance of cross-contamination might occur.
(6) The rooms used for piercings shall be enclosed and used exclusively for piercings and jewelry insertion. The room(s) used for piercing, as well as the bathroom and other common areas, shall be kept scrupulously clean and disinfected frequently. All surfaces should be nonporous, to allow them to be cleaned with bleach solution or other disinfecting liquids approved by the FDA whenever cross-contamination might occur.
(7) All jewelry contaminated with only airborne pathogens (not previously worn or contaminated) shall be disinfected with a non-hazardous hard-surface disinfectant such as Madacide. All jewelry contaminated or potentially contaminated with blood borne pathogens shall be autoclaved.
(8) All jewelry shall be autoclaved prior to use. Only the following types of jewelry shall be used in initial piercing:
a. Jewelry made of surgical implant grade stainless steel 316L, 316L or LVM ASTM F-138.
b. Solid 14 karat or higher white or yellow gold.
c. Niobium (Nb).
d. Surgical implant grade Ti6A4V ELI.
e. ASTN F-136.
f. Solid platinum.
g. Dense low porosity plastic such as Tygon or PTFE.
h. Threaded jewelry for initial piercings must have internal tapping (no threads on posts) starting from sixteen (16) gauge.
i. All jewelry must be free of nicks, scratches, burrs and polishing compounds.
j. Ring ends should be rounded.
k. Threads 1.2 mm for fourteen (14) gauge or .080 for ten (10) gauge.
l. Ear piercing guns are not adequately sterilizable and shall not be used.
m. All body piercing operators shall attend a blood borne pathogens training class, such as that given by OSHA, Red Cross, or The National Safety Council.
n. All establishments shall have separate area for employee hand washing, containing liquid soap and paper towel dispensers.
o. All establishments shall have a fully functional autoclave or sterilizer. Autoclaves are to be tested monthly for spores.
p. All clients shall receive aftercare instructions.
q. No person working in or operating any body-piercing establishment shall be under the influence of alcohol, legal or illegal substances. All health, safety, and legal standards as required by state and local authorities shall be met.
(Ord. No. 05-19, § 1, 4-18-2005)

1449:
Except as specifically defined herein, all words used in this chapter shall have their customary dictionary definition, and shall be interpreted within the context of the sentence, section, and article in which they occur. Words used in the singular include the plural and words used in the plural include the singular. Words used in the present tense include the future tense as the context may require. Words used in the future tense include the present tense as the context requires. For purposes of this chapter, the following words or terms shall be defined as follows:
Attendant means a person on duty at any commercial parking lot employed by or an agent of the owner or operator thereof.
Building includes the word "structure" and means any structure of every kind regardless of its similarity to a building.
Commercial parking lot means any facility for the parking of motorized vehicles, for which service or facility the operator charges a fee.
Commercial parking lot reservoir means an area located immediately inside the facility entrance and is to be used for the temporary storage of entering vehicles when the arrival rate exceeds the storage rate.
Commercial parking lot operator means any person, association, corporation, partnership, joint venture, or any other business arrangement or joint venture who is the owner of or is responsible for the operation of a commercial parking lot, notwithstanding whether such operator is in fact the legal owner of record of the premises itself.
Department means the City of Forest Park Department of Planning, Building and Zoning.
Environmental barriers means such barricades, chains, walls, gates, wheel stops or other like structures around the perimeter of any commercial parking lot as may be required to reasonably regulate and control the ingress to and egress from any such lot and to eliminate the encroachment of any vehicles parked on a commercial parking lot onto or over adjacent properties, including sidewalks, streets, alleys, etc.
Erected includes the words "constructed," "moved," "located," or "relocated."
Primary establishment(s) refers to the business entity or entities whose parking lot is being shared during non-business hours, with a commercial parking lot operator for the purpose of shared-use paid parking operations.
Self-parking means the patron parks his/her own vehicle, retains the keys to the vehicle, and pays the attendant or drop box upon exiting the commercial parking lot.
Shared-use lot refers to the operation of a commercial parking lot by an operator on property of which a portion is otherwise required of an establishment for the purpose of parking vehicles during that establishment's business hours.
Special events includes, but is not limited to, conventions, sporting events, concerts or any other event that generates a large volume of vehicles near the commercial parking lot at times other than normal business hours.
Ticket means a distinctive piece of paper, which shall have printed thereon a ticket number and the full name, address, and contact number for the operator or owner of the commercial parking lot.
Use fee means a fee paid by permit holders to operate as a commercial parking lot.
Valet parking means the attendant parks the vehicle and retains the key to the vehicle. Payment may be rendered upon entrance to a commercial parking lot or upon regaining the keys prior to exiting a commercial parking lot.
(Ord. No. 17-15, § 1 (Exh. A), 5-15-2017)

1452:
(a) An applicant for a commercial parking lot permit shall remit an application fee to the department. No such application shall be deemed to be complete until the full amount of such application fee has been paid. This application fee shall consist of a fixed amount as set from time-to-time by the governing body.
(b) The application fee shall be non-refundable if the permit is rejected by the department or due to circumstances that are not under the control of the city. If the applicant chooses to reapply for the permit, the applicant will have to pay another application fee.
(c) A commercial parking lot operator shall pay a quarterly use fee for each commercial parking lot that he operates within the city. Such use fee shall be in a fixed amount as set from time-to-time by the governing body to cover the costs of enforcement of this chapter, and said use fee must be paid when due in order for the continued operation of the parking facility.
(d) A commercial parking lot permit shall be valid until the last day of the calendar year in which it is issued. No earlier than forty (40) days prior to and no later than thirty (30) days from the expiration date, each commercial parking lot operator must renew its permit.
(e) Any expired commercial parking lot permit which is not renewed within three (3) months after the expiration date thereof, shall be considered void, requiring the operation of such facility to immediately cease. The operation of the commercial parking lot shall not resume until a new application is submitted to and approved by the department.
(f) If the quarterly use fee remains unpaid for a period of thirty (30) days or more after the due date thereof, the city may order the permittee of the commercial parking lot to cease operations until the unpaid use fee has been paid in full.
(Ord. No. 17-15, § 1 (Exh. A), 5-15-2017)
1454:
(a) Environmental barriers. All commercial parking lots shall contain environmental barriers in sufficient number and location as determined by the department. The permittee of such commercial parking lot shall maintain any environmental barrier located upon the property.

Special event venue means that area for which a special event permit has been issued.
Street means any right-of-way or place of whatever nature, publicly maintained and open to use for the public for purposes of motor vehicular travel. The term includes an interstate highway, a state highway, or any road.

(a) Issuance of special event permit. The director shall issue a special event permit only when, after considering the application and other information submitted by the applicant, he determines the following conditions have been met:
(1) A special event permit may be issued only after an adequate plan for crowd and traffic control, as well as security has been presented, and, when deemed necessary, employment of off-duty, uniformed Forest Park police officer(s) shall be utilized. If Forest Park police officer(s) are not available, then a P.O.S.T. certified police officer(s) may be utilized after they have been verified by the director and obtained by the producer.
(2) A special event permit may be issued only after an adequate plan for fire inspection/prevention and/or fire code enforcement and, when deemed necessary, employment of off-duty, uniformed fire personnel as approved by the Forest Park fire chief and/or his designee has been verified by the director and obtained by the producer.
(3) A special event permit may be issued only after an adequate EMS plan and, when deemed necessary, employment of off-duty medics who are state-certified EMT or paramedics, as approved by the Forest Park Fire Chief and/or his designee have been verified by the city and obtained by the producer.
(4) A special event permit may be issued only after adequate waste disposal facilities have been determined by the city and obtained by the producer.
(5) The sound level of the proposed special event will not violate any provision of the Code of Ordinances.
(6) The conduct of the proposed special event will not substantially interrupt the safe and orderly movement of other traffic contiguous to its route or place of occurrence.
(7) The conduct of the proposed special event will not require the diversion of so great a number of police officers of the city to properly police the line of movement and the areas contiguous thereto as to prevent normal police protection of the city.
(8) The concentration of individuals, animals and vehicles at assembly points of the special event will not unduly interfere with proper fire and police protection of, or ambulance service to, areas contiguous to the assembly areas.
(9) The conduct of the proposed special event will not unreasonably interfere with the movement of firefighting equipment in route to a fire.
(10) The conduct of the proposed special event is not likely to cause injury to persons or property, to provoke disorderly conduct or to promote immediate lawless activity.
(11) If a parade, the proposed special event is scheduled to move from its point of origin to its point of termination expeditiously and without unreasonable delays.
(12) The information in the application and any accompanying documents is complete and contains all information required by section 9-15-4(d) and does not contain any false material information.
(13) The applicant has remitted all applicable fees and costs required by this chapter or any other provision of the Code of Ordinances.
(b) Denial or revocation of a special event permit.
(1) The director shall deny an application for a special event permit for any of the following reasons:
a. The proposed special event will unnecessarily disrupt vehicular or pedestrian traffic within the city such that the potential disruption could not be practically remedied.
b. The proposed special event will interfere with access to fire stations or fire hydrants.
c. The location of the proposed special event will cause undue hardship to nearby businesses or residences.
d. The proposed special event will require the diversion of so many public employees that allowing the event would unreasonably deny service to the remainder of the city.
e. The information in the application and any accompanying documents fails to contain all information required by section 9-15-4(d), or contains any materially false information.
f. The proposed special event would interfere or conflict with a previously scheduled special event or with construction, maintenance or other city activities.
g. There is a documented history of problems relating to the proposed special event in the past.
h. There is a documented history that the applicant or promoter has not properly managed or paid all fees for a prior special event.
i. The proposed special event would violate section 11-1-26.
j. The producer fails to comply with any terms required by this chapter.
k. The granting of the application would violate any provision of this chapter, would violate any provision of the Code of Ordinances, or would violate any provision of Georgia or United States law.

a. The director discovers that the application for such permit failed to contain all information required by section 9-15-4(d) or contained any materially false information.
b. The producer failed to comply with all terms and conditions of the permit.
c. The producer failed to arrange or adequately remit all required fees, deposits, insurance or bonds to the city.
